title: A virtual reality eyes disease experience for nursing students
author: Parozzi, Ferrara, et al.

steps.title: Obtain authorizations and administer questionnaire
steps.instruction: Secure all required ethical and institutional authorizations, then have each student complete the initial questionnaire assessing prior knowledge, opinions, and experiences with eye‑care diseases and disorders.

steps.title: Seat student and give VR safety instructions
steps.instruction: Place the enrolled student alone in a swivel chair at the centre of the room, ensure they cannot touch surrounding objects, and provide strict instructions: they may rotate the chair 360° and move their head freely but must not stand; they must inform the educator of any physically unpleasant sensations during the virtual experience.

steps.title: Fit VR headset and start experience
steps.instruction: Assist the student in wearing the VR head‑mount device, ensure the app’s sound is turned off, and then initiate the virtual reality experience.

steps.title: Run normal view then eye‑disease view
steps.instruction: Present a normal 360° scene for 30 seconds; after that, switch to the eye‑disease view for an additional 30 seconds, showing the same everyday scene from the perspective of a glaucoma patient (bus‑stop setting) or a cataract patient (car setting).

steps.title: Monitor student and intervene only if needed
steps.instruction: During the 3‑D experience, refrain from communicating with the student except to announce the view change; continuously note the student’s movements, externalizations, and reactions. Intervene only if the student makes dangerous movements or reports physical discomfort, in which case terminate the experience immediately.

steps.title: Conduct post‑experience interview
steps.instruction: After the VR session, carry out a semi‑structured interview (validated for content), record the interview, then transcribe it for later analysis.

steps.title: Analyze interview data with NVivo
steps.instruction: Two nursing Ph.D. researchers with >15 years teaching experience will perform data analysis using NVivo software, applying the Colaizzi qualitative analysis approach.
